clue.text: Footballer seems to have a messy face

definitions.text: seems to have a messy face

blocks.note: first meaning: a player who runs the ball past opponents with small touches

blocks.clueFragment: seems to have a messy face
blocks.note: second meaning: someone who lets saliva run down the chin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a muddy player; the two readings are a skilful ball-runner and a slobberer.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word names both a player skilled at close ball control and a person who drools, leaving the chin wet.

clue.text: One wants a journey in another place

blocks.note: one is the indefinite article a
a way is a route or journey; the article is absorbed

explanation.surface: Someone longs to travel somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes being absent, elsewhere, not at home.

clue.text: Grit is churned up when river comes in view

indicators.note: anything churned up is stirred and tumbled out of its order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Muddy gravel stirred up signals that a river is near.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tigris is the great river of Iraq, one of the two rivers of Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Urge on the chief, a boffin through and through

blocks.note: to egg on is to urge on
the head is the chief

explanation.surface: Someone spurs on the boss, who is a thoroughgoing intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or brainy expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an intellectual, a thoroughly bookish or scientific type.

clue.text: Pasta for Mother, Gigi! I'll come later

indicators.note: coming later means this word is placed after the others, at the end

blocks.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
Leslie Caron starred as Gigi in the 1958 film musical
the pronoun I, with the contracted will dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tells their mother and Gigi to start on the pasta while they follow later.
explanation.walkthrough: Gigi stands for the actress who played her, Leslie Caron.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is short tubular Italian pasta.

clue.text: Rustling hip-swinger must become much straighter

indicators.note: straightening out something that swings means rearranging it into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A swaying dancer in a rustling skirt is told to stand up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves or silk rustling make a soft whispering sound, so the two adjectives match.

clue.text: For worldwide newsgroups, do not fish with line!

blocks.note: first meaning: the old global internet discussion network
second meaning, split in two words: an instruction to employ a mesh instead of rod and line

explanation.surface: Advice to an angler to give up the rod and line.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition only works read as two words, an instruction to the angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet was the worldwide distributed system of discussion newsgroups that predates web forums.

clue.text: Poet with brother having kept behind

indicators.note: behind places the second piece after the first

blocks.note: Br is the abbreviation for brother
owning means having or keeping

explanation.surface: A poet and his brother stayed back somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning, and Elizabeth Barrett Browning, were Victorian poets.

clue.text: Pains of a child in turning tide you'll find

indicators.note: turning round means reading the word for tide backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the tide stands for the sea itself
ch is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child caught in the turning tide suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tide stands loosely for the body of water it moves, and the 'a' in the clue is only surface glue, since the reversed water supplies its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Aches are dull continuous pains, the plural noun matching.

clue.text: Comply with order at the end of day

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A command to be followed by close of business.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to do as instructed, to comply with a rule or order.

clue.text: Training a dog, or practising a play

blocks.note: first meaning: drilling an animal by making it repeat its routine
second meaning: running through a stage show before performance

explanation.walkthrough: The verb can mean drilling anyone by repetition, so it stretches to putting a dog through its paces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are about repeated drilling, of an animal's tricks or of actors' lines.

clue.text: Staple, perhaps, that common folk might lick

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the given word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A basic food so good that ordinary people would lick it off the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a tongue-in-cheek description: only the unmannered lick their dishes clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes are licked clean by those without table manners, so the crockery fits the playful description.

clue.text: Poor boy with nothing gets a pass that's fine

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: a ticket is a pass for entry
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A penniless lad gets a free pass and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned British slang for all in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo is a dated British colloquialism meaning all right, going smoothly.

clue.text: Cupid turned fish-eater after a tick

indicators.note: turned round means the animal's name is read backwards
after puts the animal behind the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
a tick and a mo are both a moment
the otter feeds on fish

explanation.surface: The god of love has suddenly taken up a fishy diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Tick and mo are British informal words for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a cherub or little Cupid in Italian art.

clue.text: This spider (weaver, Greek) can hear like that

indicators.note: like that suggests the words can be made into that by being reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spider with sharp hearing, described as a Greek weaver.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Arachne, a mortal weaver, challenged Athena and was turned into a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachne is the mythical Greek weaver transformed into the first spider.

clue.text: Futile when Tory's following up a gun

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the phrase is read from the bottom upwards
following puts the party member after the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a Tory is a British Conservative; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician pursues a gunman, to no avail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, worthless and useless.

clue.text: Short, very small young child seen in a hat

indicators.note: in places the child inside the headgear

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat
a mite is a tiny child

explanation.surface: A tiny toddler appears in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The child goes in after the second letter of the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited supply and short supply both mean restricted in quantity.

clue.text: It's time to choose when baby-kissing's done

definitions.text: It's time to choose when baby-kissing's done

blocks.note: surface reading: a fond moment once the cuddles are over
setter's reading: politicians kiss babies while canvassing, and then voters pick a winner

explanation.walkthrough: Kissing babies is the cliché of campaigning politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote follows the campaign, when the public chooses its representatives.

clue.text: Take back the car, but not on motorway

definitions.text: the car, but not on motorway

blocks.note: first meaning: overturn or withdraw a decision

blocks.clueFragment: the car, but not on motorway
blocks.note: second meaning: drive backwards, never allowed on a motorway

explanation.walkthrough: A motorway is a British high-speed highway, where backing up is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both revoking a decision and driving a vehicle backwards.

clue.text: This coastal bird could show a leg with ease

indicators.note: could show suggests the words might be rearranged to display something else

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoreline bird stretches a leg effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a large fish-eating raptor that lives along coasts.

clue.text: Please sort it out and then just slip away

indicators.note: sorting something out rearranges it into order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to fix a problem quickly and then leave quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by unnoticed, slipping away.

clue.text: We rang to solve The Ring, his masterpiece

indicators.note: to solve something is to work its parts out into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone phoned to make sense of a great operatic work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring is the four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner composed the Ring cycle, widely held to be his greatest work.

clue.text: Twisting her wit will make you droop or fade

indicators.note: twisting distorts the order of what follows

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's sharp tongue leaves you deflated.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants wither as they shrivel, sag and lose colour.

clue.text: Affluent life described in a glib way

blocks.note: glib means facile, easy
way appears in road names, like street

explanation.surface: A life of wealth portrayed superficially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a glib way' reads as a manner, but glib and way are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort and prosperity.

clue.text: A chateau where this bugbear has to stay

indicators.note: where this points to a place in which the thing sits inside a word

blocks.note: letters two to five of chateau

explanation.surface: A grand French house where a dreaded guest must lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a pet hate, a thing one particularly dislikes.

clue.text: Expectancy when many a film he made

blocks.note: first meaning: a feeling of expectation
second meaning: Bob, the comedian who starred in the Road films

explanation.walkthrough: Bob Hope made many films, including the Road series with Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an expectation of good things and the surname of a prolific Hollywood comic actor.

clue.text: Trail of an animal that's small and lowly

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
lowly and poor both mean humble

explanation.surface: Tracking a little, humble creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track, scent or droppings left by a wild animal.

clue.text: Bitch holding record may be Border collie

indicators.note: holding means the female dog wraps around the disc

blocks.note: a bitch is a female dog
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A female dog clutching a record could be a collie.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, signalled by 'may be'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Border collie is a breed used to herd flocks, an example of a working farm dog.
